text:
tim_support: Customer cust-omega reports embeddings size flip after we pinned to a variant. They say most responses are 1024-d vectors but ~1/5 of responses come back as 512-d. Started after pinned upgrade yesterday. Anyone seen this? :eyes:

sara_cs: Oof. Can you paste a failing request_id + the minimal payload? region? routing tier?

tim_support: Minimal payload and one failing response below. Happened on us-west-2, reserved tier. request_id: req_abc123. Example request:

```http
POST /v1/embeddings
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_abc123

{"model":"embed-large","input":["a","b","c"]}
```

And the (trimmed) response we returned to customer: 

```json
{"object":"list","data":[{"embedding":[0.001,0.002,...],"index":0},{"embedding":[0.003,0.004,...],"index":1},{"embedding":[0.005,0.006,...],"index":2}],"model":"embed-large"}
```

Note: the arrays above are placeholders — in the real response the first two embedding arrays had length 1024, the third array length 512. I can attach the full payload if needed.

alex_infra: Pinged infra logs for req_abc123. Saw router warning: "variant_mismatch: pinned->fallback embed-large-int8 used for shard s3 due to capacity". That suggests routing fell back to a quantized variant.

mike_ml: We did onboard embed-large-int8 as a size/latency optimization yesterday and toggled it as a compatible variant for the embed-large alias. It should preserve vector width, but the int8 conversion pipeline also trimmed some final projection dims in one early conversion commit. Not expected, but plausible.

sara_cs: tim, does customer see this only when batch size >= 3 or only intermittently? Any pattern on batch size / throughput?

tim_support: Customer says frequency spikes when they send larger batches (>=8) or during high-throughput bursts. I also have a second request id where we saw the same: req_def456.

alex_infra: Correlating req_abc123 and req_def456 — both hit the batching path that selects a lower-memory node pool. Those nodes have the int8 variant hot; router log shows fallback to embed-large-int8 at commit hash a1b2c3 for those requests. The int8 build currently emits 512-d vectors due to the conversion bug.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: embed-large-int8 -> us-west-2 completed at 2026-03-01T02:12:43Z (canary, 20% nodes).

jlee: We should block that variant from being used for pinned customers until we fix it. Temporary routing rule: if request has X-Customer-Pinned true or is under reserved tier, prefer non-quantized commithash. I'll apply a rule scoping pinned customer IDs.

mike_ml: I'll open an urgent PR to re-run conversion with correct projection and add a regression test asserting embedding length == model.config.hidden_size. Also adding a detection alert to tests in the model onboarding job.

alex_infra: For immediate mitigation: 1) ops: apply jlee's routing rule; 2) support: offer rollback to previous pinned commit (stable-2026-02-28) to affected customers; 3) engineering: hotfix quant conversion.

tim_support: I've notified cust-omega and offered rollback to stable-2026-02-28 — they accepted. Putting them on a short maintenance hold.

sara_cs: Thanks — please paste the rollback request ids when done so CS can close the escalation.

mike_ml: Rolling back pinned alias for affected accounts now. I will update once rollback finished and include a postmortem with root cause and fix planned.

tim_support: Rollback confirmed for cust-omega, new request id for rollback operation: req_rollback_901. Customer validated vectors are back to 1024 for repeated checks.

jlee: Routing rule in place to prevent embed-large-int8 for pinned/reserved tiers until next sign-off.

mike_ml: Follow-up actions: fix conversion, add unit/regression tests, stop auto-assigning int8 variant to alias until dims validated. Will target a patch release in next 24h.

tim_support: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all. :pray:
